rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (base_speed 0.9, sensors y 0.07, kp 1.4, kd 0.5; score 683.7, the best so far). The oval finished 20/20 at 1.99 s. The s-bend finished 20/20 at 2.25 s, with max_error 0.028 and oscillation 0.29. The slalom still went off_track in all 20 runs, but progress rose from 0.311 to 0.392 and max_error stayed near the 0.06 m limit (mean 0.0646). The speed reduction therefore moved the slalom, which supports the speed-limited reading. The Evaluator's stale review (written before iteration 6 raced) says that if slalom progress rises above 0.31 with the oval still at 20/20, try base_speed 0.85 provided the s-bend completion_time stays under 2.9 s. Both conditions hold: 2.25 s is well under 2.9 s. Change: base_speed 0.9 to 0.85, with everything else unchanged (kp 1.4, ki 0, kd 0.5, y 0.07, x positions, 16 mm footprints, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss last_direction). This is a single-variable step. Expected result: slalom progress rises further, perhaps to about 0.45 to 0.5, with the oval still at 20/20 (about 2.0 s) and the s-bend near 2.4 to 2.5 s. Risks: if the s-bend completion_time exceeds 2.9 s or s-bend finishes fall below 17/20, return base_speed to 0.9. If slalom progress stalls near 0.39 at 0.85, the next lever is sensor reach at the sharpest bend (y 0.075), or a modest kd change if oscillation rises. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness.
